1. Allowed, subject to all just exception.

This is a petition under Section 397 read with Section 482 Cr.P.C.,1973 seeking quashing of the order dated 07.11.2023 passed by learned ASJ (FTSC)(RC), District East, Karkardooma Courts,
Delhi framing charges passed under Section 376 IPC 1860 against the petitioner and order on charge dated 07.12.2023.
4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner and the complainant were in a relationship.
The complainant threatened the petitioner of filing a criminal case against him of having committed offence under Section 376 IPC 1860 on the pretext of promise of marriage.
5. It is submitted that subsequently, on 26.10.2014 the parties i.e. the petitioner and the complainant got married as per Muslim rites and customs.
This is a digitally signed order.

It is further submitted that on account of said marriage, the aforesaid complaint was withdrawn by the complainant.

6. Learned counsel further submits that subsequently since the parties were having temperamental differences, they entered into a divorce deed i.e. talaq nama in accordance with Muslim rites and customs on 04.03.2015.
Learned counsel further submits that accordingly, the statement of the parties was also recorded in Court.
As per the statement the petitioner had agreed to pay to the complainant a total sum of Rs. 15 Lakhs as full and final settlement.

She further submits that it is only after the statement was recorded; the divorce having been granted; and the complainant having accepted a sum of Rs. 15 Lakhs as full and final settlement on account of the settlement terms for the divorce, the complainant malafidely had reinitiated the complaint under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. for the alleged offence of Section 376 IPC alleged to have been committed prior to entering into the marriage with the petitioner.
7.
Learned MM had directed registration of an FIR No. 446/2015 under Sections 376/506/34/313/328 IPC 1860 registered at PS Jagat Puri, Delhi against the petitioner and his parents.
8. The present petition arises from the said FIR.
Learned counsel further submits that in the interregnum, unfortunately the mother of the petitioner had expired and as such the criminal case qua her had abated.
She also further submits that the father of the petitioner was also discharged by the learned MM vide the aforesaid impugned order.

9. On the aforesaid basis, the learned Counsel submits that even if the entire material, available with the learned Sessions Judge is considered, no charges under Section 376 IPC could have been made out keeping in view This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/12/2023 at 23:51:20 the peculiar facts of the case.
10. Issue notice.
Notice accepted by Mr. Hemant Mehla, learned APP for the State.
11. Let status report be filed within a period of 04 weeks from today with an advance copy to the learned counsel for the petitioner.
In terms of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jagjeet Singh and Others vs. Ashish Mishra Alias Monu and Another (2022) 9 SCC 321, let notice be also issued to the complainant/victim.

13. Reply be filed qua the stay application before the next date of hearing.
